title: Me dijo que vendría: reported speech
summary: Pass on what people said, asked and asked you to do: tenses step back, questions take si or keep their question word, and here and now become there and then.
focus: Reported speech: backshift of tenses, reported questions and requests, and shifting time and place words
content:
## Reporting what someone said

To pass on someone's words you need a reporting verb and **que**: **decir** (to say, tell), **contar** (to tell, recount), **explicar** (to explain), **comentar** (to mention), **añadir** (to add), **prometer** (to promise). Questions take **preguntar**; requests take **pedir**.

If the reporting verb is in the present, nothing shifts:

- «Estoy cansada.» → **Dice que está cansada.** (She says she's tired.)

If it is in the past (**dijo, contó, explicó…**), the reported verb usually steps one place back in time. This is the *backshift*:

- «Estoy cansada.» → **Dijo que estaba cansada.** (She said she was tired.)

## The backshift table

| Direct speech | Reported after **dijo que…** |
|---|---|
| present: «**Voy** al médico.» | imperfect: **iba** al médico |
| preterite: «**Fui** al médico.» | pluperfect: **había ido** (**fue** is also heard in speech) |
| present perfect: «**He ido**.» | pluperfect: **había ido** |
| future: «**Iré**.» | conditional: **iría** |
| imperfect / conditional: «**Iba**.» «**Iría**.» | no change: **iba**, **iría** |
| imperative: «**Ven**.» | **que** + imperfect subjunctive: **que viniera** |

**Still true?** Then you may keep the present: **Me dijo que es de Sevilla** (she still is). **Era** is just as correct; it tells the story from the past.

## Questions and requests

- Yes/no questions are reported with **si** (*whether*, no accent): «¿Tienes coche?» → **Me preguntó si tenía coche.**
- Questions with a question word keep it, accent and all: «¿Dónde vives?» → **Me preguntó dónde vivía.** «¿Qué quieres?» → **Me preguntó qué quería.**
- Orders and requests become **pedir que** or **decir que** + subjunctive; after a past verb, the imperfect subjunctive:
  - «Llámame.» → **Me pidió que la llamara.** (She asked me to call her.)
  - «No toquéis nada.» → **Nos dijo que no tocáramos nada.** (He told us not to touch anything.)

**Decir que** + indicative passes on information; **decir que** + subjunctive passes on an order.

## Here becomes there: time and place words

Words that point at the speaker's *here and now* shift when you report them somewhere else or later:

| Direct | Reported |
|---|---|
| **aquí** | **allí** |
| **hoy** | **aquel día** |
| **ayer** | **el día anterior** |
| **mañana** | **al día siguiente** |
| **ahora** | **entonces** |
| **este / esta** | **ese / esa** (or **aquel / aquella**) |

- «Volveré aquí mañana.» → **Dijo que volvería allí al día siguiente.** (He said he would come back there the next day.)

Persons shift too: «**mi** hermano» → **su hermano**.

vocabulary.example: Mi abuela nos contó que de joven había vivido en Cuba.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandmother told us that she had lived in Cuba as a young woman.

vocabulary.example: El camarero nos preguntó si queríamos postre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The waiter asked us whether we wanted dessert.

vocabulary.example: El jefe me pidió que revisara el informe.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The boss asked me to check the report.

vocabulary.example: La guía nos explicó que el museo cerraba los lunes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The guide explained to us that the museum closed on Mondays.

vocabulary.example: Pablo comentó que el piso nuevo era muy luminoso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Pablo mentioned that the new flat was very bright.

vocabulary.example: Luego añadió que no hacía falta reservar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Then he added that there was no need to book.

vocabulary.example: Me prometió que me devolvería el libro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She promised me she would give the book back.

vocabulary.meaning: to let someone know, to warn
vocabulary.example: Nos avisó de que el tren saldría con retraso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He let us know that the train would leave late.

vocabulary.meaning: the next day, the following day
vocabulary.example: Dijeron que vendrían al día siguiente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: They said they would come the next day.

vocabulary.meaning: the day before, the previous day
vocabulary.example: Me contó que había llegado el día anterior.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She told me she had arrived the day before.

vocabulary.example: Explicó que aquel día no tenía tiempo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He explained that he didn't have time that day.

vocabulary.example: Te dejo un recado: dice Carmen que la llames.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here's a message for you: Carmen says to call her.

quiz.prompt: Last Friday Ana said: «Hoy estoy agotada.» → Ana me dijo que aquel día ___ agotada.
quiz.explanation: After a past reporting verb the present steps back to the imperfect, and hoy becomes aquel día: 'Ana me dijo que aquel día estaba agotada.'
hints: Present in direct speech becomes the imperfect after dijo.

quiz.prompt: Luis: «Iré a la reunión.» → Luis me prometió que ___ a la reunión. (ir)
quiz.explanation: The future in direct speech becomes the conditional after a past reporting verb: iré → iría.
hints: Ir in the conditional, él form.

quiz.prompt: Marta: «Perdí las llaves ayer.» → Marta me contó que ___ las llaves el día anterior.
quiz.explanation: In careful reported speech a preterite becomes the pluperfect (había + participle): perdí → había perdido. In everyday speech the preterite (perdió, as at B1) is also heard. Ayer becomes el día anterior.
hints: The past before the past is the pluperfect.

quiz.prompt: Mi madre: «Ven a las ocho.» → Mi madre me pidió que ___ a las ocho. (venir)
quiz.explanation: A reported order takes que + subjunctive; after the past pidió it is the imperfect subjunctive: vinieron → viniera.
hints: An order after a past verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with si (whether), without an accent: 'Me preguntó si tenía coche.'
hints: A yes/no question is introduced by whether.

quiz.prompt: «¿Dónde vives?» → Me preguntó ___ vivía. (keep the question word)
quiz.explanation: A question with a question word keeps it, accent included: 'Me preguntó dónde vivía.'
hints: The question word stays, with its accent.

quiz.prompt: Last week Pedro said: «Volveré mañana.» → Pedro dijo que volvería ___.
quiz.explanation: Reported a week later, mañana no longer means tomorrow: it becomes al día siguiente.
hints: Mañana from the speaker's point of view becomes the next day.

quiz.prompt: The teacher said: «El agua hierve a cien grados.» → La profesora nos explicó que el agua ___ a cien grados. (a fact that is still true)
quiz.explanation: A fact that is still true can keep the present after a past reporting verb: 'nos explicó que el agua hierve a cien grados'. Hervía would also be correct, but not the conditional or the pluperfect.

quiz.prompt: Rocío, about her village: «Aquí se come muy bien.» → Rocío comentó que ___ se comía muy bien. (aquí → ?)
quiz.explanation: Reported from somewhere else, aquí becomes allí: 'Rocío comentó que allí se comía muy bien.'

conversations.title: The landlord's call
conversations.scenario: Elena tells her flatmate Javier what their landlord said on the phone.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: El casero. Me dijo que pasaría el jueves a revisar la caldera.
lines.meaning: The landlord. He said he would come by on Thursday to check the boiler.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿El jueves? ¿Le explicaste que trabajamos los dos?
lines.meaning: Thursday? Did you explain to him that we both work?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, y me preguntó si alguno de nosotros podía quedarse en casa.
lines.meaning: Yes, and he asked me whether one of us could stay at home.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Le dije que lo hablaría contigo. También me pidió que le enviáramos una foto de la caldera.
lines.meaning: I told him I'd talk it over with you. He also asked us to send him a photo of the boiler.
lines.note: A request takes que + imperfect subjunctive

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: OK. Did he mention anything about the rent?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, añadió que el año que viene lo subiría un poco.
lines.meaning: Yes, he added that next year he would put it up a little.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: What a surprise! And did he tell you how much?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No. Me prometió que nos lo explicaría todo el jueves.
lines.meaning: No. He promised he would explain it all to us on Thursday.

listening.text: Dice que está cansado.
listening.meaning: He says he's tired.

listening.text: Mi hermano dijo que tenía hambre.
listening.meaning: My brother said he was hungry.

listening.text: Nos preguntaron si queríamos más café.
listening.meaning: They asked us whether we wanted more coffee.

listening.text: El médico me explicó que no era nada grave.
listening.meaning: The doctor explained to me that it was nothing serious.

listening.text: Mi vecina me pidió que le regara las plantas.
listening.meaning: My neighbour asked me to water her plants.

listening.text: Me contó que había vivido tres años en Lisboa.
listening.meaning: She told me she had lived in Lisbon for three years.

listening.text: La abogada añadió que al día siguiente firmarían el contrato.
listening.meaning: The lawyer added that they would sign the contract the next day.
listening.note: New word: la abogada = the lawyer.

listening.text: El conductor nos avisó de que el autobús no pararía en aquella calle.
listening.meaning: The driver warned us that the bus would not stop in that street.

guide.tip: Ask when the words were said. If the reporting verb is in the past, step each verb one place back unless the fact is still true.

bites.title: Past verb, step back
bites.rule: After dijo, contó or explicó, the reported verb steps back: the present becomes the imperfect, the future becomes the conditional, and the preterite or perfect becomes the pluperfect.
bites.example: «Voy al cine.» → Dijo que iba al cine.
bites.example_meaning: 'I'm going to the cinema.' → He said he was going to the cinema.

bites.title: Orders become subjunctive
bites.rule: A reported order or request takes que + subjunctive; after a past verb, the imperfect subjunctive: ven becomes me pidió que viniera.
bites.example_meaning: She asked me to wait for her.

bites.title: Si or the question word
bites.rule: Yes/no questions are reported with si (no accent); other questions keep their question word with its accent: qué, dónde, cuándo.
bites.example: Me preguntó si tenía hambre y qué quería comer.
bites.example_meaning: He asked me whether I was hungry and what I wanted to eat.

bites.title: Here and now move
bites.rule: Hoy becomes aquel día, mañana becomes al día siguiente, ayer becomes el día anterior, aquí becomes allí and este becomes ese. A fact that is still true needs no backshift.
bites.example: Dijo que volvería allí al día siguiente.
bites.example_meaning: He said he would come back there the next day.

sorts.title: Which tense after dijo que?
sorts.why: The present becomes the imperfect, the preterite or perfect becomes the pluperfect, the future becomes the conditional, and the imperative becomes que + imperfect subjunctive.

sorts.title: Si or the question word?
sorts.why: Yes/no questions are reported with si; questions with qué, dónde, cuándo… keep that word.

spots.sentence: Ana dijo que vendrá al día siguiente.
spots.why: After a past reporting verb, the future becomes the conditional.

spots.sentence: Me preguntó sí quería un café.
spots.why: Reported yes/no questions use si (whether), no accent.

spots.sentence: Me pidió que la llamaba por la tarde.
spots.why: A reported request takes the imperfect subjunctive after pidió.

spots.sentence: Nos contó que aquel día ha perdido el tren.
spots.why: A perfect in direct speech becomes the pluperfect when reported in the past.
The question word keeps its accent in a reported question.

builds.text: Me dijo que estaba muy ocupada.
builds.meaning: She told me she was very busy.
We asked him whether he wanted to come.

builds.text: Nos pidió que habláramos más bajo.
builds.meaning: She asked us to speak more quietly.

builds.text: Prometió que lo haría al día siguiente.
builds.meaning: He promised he would do it the next day.

realm.content:
## El estilo indirecto en Eldmark

In Eldmark, news travels by herald and tavern gossip. The quest-giver **dijo que el orco vivía en la mazmorra**, the paladin **prometió que volvería al día siguiente**, and the innkeeper **te pidió que pagaras** before going upstairs. Past reporting verb, one step back.

vocabulary.example: El enano nos contó que había encontrado oro en Deepanvil.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarf told us he had found gold in Deepanvil.

vocabulary.example: La maga me pidió que le trajera tres raíces del Bosque Umbrío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage asked me to bring her three roots from the Bosque Umbrío.

vocabulary.example: El paladín prometió que protegería la posada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The paladin promised he would protect the inn.

vocabulary.example: El guardia me preguntó si llevaba armas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The guard asked me whether I was carrying weapons.

vocabulary.example: El cazador dijo que partiría hacia Frostmarch al día siguiente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The hunter said he would set off for Frostmarch the next day.

vocabulary.example: El heraldo anunció que el rey visitaría Highgate.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The herald announced that the king would visit Highgate.

vocabulary.example: El pergamino decía que el botín estaba bajo el puente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The scroll said that the loot was under the bridge.

vocabulary.example: La posadera dijo que no quedaban habitaciones.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The innkeeper said there were no rooms left.

bites.title: Rumores de taberna
bites.rule: In tavern gossip a past reporting verb moves every verb one step back: «El minotauro duerme» → dijo que el minotauro dormía; «Iré» → dijo que iría.
bites.example: El cazador dijo que el jefe dormía en la cueva.
bites.example_meaning: The hunter said that the boss was sleeping in the cave.

listening.text: Dijo que el orco dormía.
listening.meaning: He said the orc was sleeping.

listening.text: La elfa preguntó dónde estaba la posada.
listening.meaning: The elf asked where the inn was.

listening.text: El heraldo anunció que el rey llegaría pronto.
listening.meaning: The herald announced that the king would arrive soon.
listening.note: New word: el heraldo = the herald.

listening.text: El enano me pidió que le afilara el hacha.
listening.meaning: The dwarf asked me to sharpen his axe.

listening.text: El minotauro nos contó que había perdido su montura.
listening.meaning: The minotaur told us he had lost his mount.

builds.text: El posadero prometió que guardaría la montura.
builds.meaning: The innkeeper promised he would look after the mount.

builds.text: La maga preguntó si estábamos listos.
builds.meaning: The mage asked whether we were ready.

spots.sentence: El paladín prometió que volverá al día siguiente.
spots.why: After a past reporting verb, the future becomes the conditional.

spots.sentence: El guardia me pidió que le enseño el pase.
spots.why: A reported request takes the imperfect subjunctive after pidió.

sorts.title: Rumores de la posada
sorts.why: Reported later, the present becomes the imperfect and the future becomes the conditional.

quiz.prompt: El heraldo: «El rey llegará a Highgate.» → El heraldo anunció que el rey ___ a Highgate al día siguiente.
quiz.explanation: The future becomes the conditional after a past reporting verb, and al día siguiente fixes the past point of view: llegaría.

quiz.prompt: La elfa: «¿Dónde está la posada?» → La elfa me preguntó ___ estaba la posada.
quiz.explanation: The question word stays, accent included: 'me preguntó dónde estaba la posada'.

conversations.title: News from the herald
conversations.scenario: At the inn in Highgate, the hunter Mirna tells the warrior Bastián what the herald told her.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bastián, ayer hablé con el heraldo de Highgate.
lines.meaning: Bastián, yesterday I spoke to the herald of Highgate.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: And what did he tell you?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me dijo que un minotauro vigilaba la mazmorra del Bosque Umbrío.
lines.meaning: He told me that a minotaur was guarding the dungeon in the Bosque Umbrío.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Did he explain what was inside?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, añadió que el botín era enorme, pero que la puerta estaba cerrada.
lines.meaning: Yes, he added that the loot was huge, but that the door was locked.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: And did he ask you whether we wanted to go?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me pidió que reuniéramos un grupo antes del amanecer.
lines.meaning: He asked us to gather a party before dawn.
lines.note: A request takes que + imperfect subjunctive

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues avísale de que saldremos mañana al amanecer.
lines.meaning: Then let him know we'll set off tomorrow at dawn.

meadowbrook.content:
## El estilo indirecto en Meadowbrook

News in Meadowbrook travels from the seed shop to the tavern. Rosa **dijo que las semillas de fresa llegarían el lunes**, Leo **contó que había pescado un pez enorme**, and the mayor **nos pidió que decoráramos la plaza** for the festival. Past verb, one step back.

vocabulary.example: Leo nos contó que había pescado un salmón enorme en el río.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo told us he had caught a huge salmon in the river.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde nos pidió que trajéramos calabazas al festival.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor asked us to bring pumpkins to the festival.

vocabulary.example: Rosa prometió que me guardaría semillas de maíz.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa promised she would keep some corn seeds for me.

vocabulary.example: Nora me preguntó cuándo se cosechaban las fresas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora asked me when strawberries were harvested.

vocabulary.example: Rosa me avisó de que la tienda cerraría pronto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa let me know that the shop would close soon.

vocabulary.example: El chisme de la taberna decía que el alcalde bailaría en el festival.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The tavern gossip said the mayor would dance at the festival.

vocabulary.example: Rosa dijo que las semillas de calabaza se habían agotado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa said the pumpkin seeds had sold out.

vocabulary.example: El pescador dijo que el río estaba muy frío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The fisherman said the river was very cold.

bites.title: Noticias de la granja
bites.rule: When a neighbour's words are passed on later, the tenses step back: «Plantaré maíz» → Nora dijo que plantaría maíz.
bites.example: Nora dijo que plantaría maíz en primavera.
bites.example_meaning: Nora said she would plant corn in spring.

listening.text: Rosa dijo que estaba cansada.
listening.meaning: Rosa said she was tired.

listening.text: Leo preguntó si hacía buen tiempo.
listening.meaning: Leo asked whether the weather was good.

listening.text: Nora contó que la vaca se había escapado.
listening.meaning: Nora said the cow had escaped.

listening.text: El alcalde nos pidió que limpiáramos la plaza.
listening.meaning: The mayor asked us to clean the square.

listening.text: Rosa me avisó de que el granero estaba lleno.
listening.meaning: Rosa let me know that the barn was full.
listening.note: New word: el granero = the barn.

builds.text: Nora dijo que cosecharía las fresas.
builds.meaning: Nora said she would harvest the strawberries.

builds.text: El alcalde preguntó si vendríamos al festival.
builds.meaning: The mayor asked whether we would come to the festival.

spots.sentence: Leo me contó que aquel día ha pescado tres truchas.
spots.why: A perfect in direct speech becomes the pluperfect when reported in the past.

spots.sentence: Rosa me pidió que la ayudo en la tienda.
spots.why: A reported request takes the imperfect subjunctive after pidió.

sorts.title: ¿Si o palabra interrogativa?
sorts.why: Yes/no questions are reported with si; questions with cuándo, dónde, quién… keep that word.

quiz.prompt: Nora: «Plantaré calabazas.» → Nora dijo que al día siguiente ___ calabazas.
quiz.explanation: The future becomes the conditional after a past reporting verb: plantaré → plantaría.

quiz.prompt: El alcalde: «¿Vendréis al festival?» → El alcalde nos preguntó ___ iríamos al festival.
quiz.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with si, without an accent. Notice that vendréis also becomes iríamos: the point of view changes.
hints: A yes/no question is introduced by whether.

rustwake.content:
## El estilo indirecto en el páramo

Outside la cúpula, news comes over the **radiorreloj**. El capataz Ruiz **dijo que se acercaba una tormenta de ceniza**, Marta **me preguntó si tenía tuercas**, and Leo **nos pidió que no bebiéramos agua sin filtrar**. Past reporting verb, one step back.

vocabulary.example: El radiorreloj nos avisó de que se acercaba una tormenta de ceniza.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The wrist radio warned us that an ash storm was approaching.

vocabulary.example: Marta me preguntó cuántas tuercas llevaba.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta asked me how many nuts I was carrying.

vocabulary.example: Leo prometió que me arreglaría el radiorreloj.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo promised he would fix my wrist radio.

vocabulary.example: El capataz Ruiz explicó que la cúpula cerraba al anochecer.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Foreman Ruiz explained that the Dome closed at nightfall.

vocabulary.example: Leo nos contó que había encontrado un disco en el centro comercial.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo told us he had found a record in the mall.

vocabulary.example: El aviso decía que no saliéramos de noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The notice said we shouldn't go out at night.

vocabulary.example: La buscadora dijo que el taller estaba vacío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The scavenger said the workshop was empty.

vocabulary.example: Ruiz anunció que la tormenta de ceniza había pasado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Ruiz announced that the ash storm had passed.

bites.title: Mensajes del radiorreloj
bites.rule: Radio messages reported later step back: «Hay polvo» → dijo que había polvo; «Cerrad las puertas» → nos pidió que cerráramos las puertas.
bites.example: El capataz nos pidió que cerráramos las puertas.
bites.example_meaning: The foreman asked us to close the doors.

listening.text: Marta dijo que no tenía agua.
listening.meaning: Marta said she had no water.

listening.text: Leo preguntó dónde estaba la gasolinera.
listening.meaning: Leo asked where the petrol station was.

listening.text: El robot dijo que los tomates estaban listos.
listening.meaning: The robot said the tomatoes were ready.

listening.text: Marta me pidió que le trajera chatarra del taller.
listening.meaning: Marta asked me to bring her scrap metal from the workshop.
listening.note: New word: la chatarra = scrap metal.

listening.text: Ruiz nos avisó de que llegaba una tormenta de ceniza.
listening.meaning: Ruiz warned us that an ash storm was coming.

builds.text: Leo dijo que estaba en el taller.
builds.meaning: Leo said he was in the workshop.

builds.text: El capataz prometió que repararía la antena.
builds.meaning: The foreman promised he would repair the antenna.

spots.sentence: Marta me preguntó cuantas tuercas tenía.
spots.why: The question word keeps its accent in a reported question.

spots.sentence: Ruiz nos pidió que no salimos de la cúpula.
spots.why: A reported request takes the imperfect subjunctive after pidió.

sorts.title: Del radiorreloj al relato
sorts.why: Reported later, the present becomes the imperfect, the perfect becomes the pluperfect and the future becomes the conditional.

quiz.prompt: Ruiz: «Cerrad la puerta.» → Ruiz nos pidió que ___ la puerta. (cerrar)
quiz.explanation: A reported order after a past verb takes the imperfect subjunctive: cerraron → cerráramos, with an accent on the nosotros form.
hints: An order after pidió takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Leo: «Encontré un disco ayer.» → Leo me contó que ___ un disco el día anterior.
quiz.explanation: In careful reported speech a preterite becomes the pluperfect: encontré → había encontrado. In everyday speech the preterite (encontró) is also heard. Ayer becomes el día anterior.
hints: The past before the past is the pluperfect.
